newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia toughens check on Bangladeshis at border.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia toughens check on Bangladeshis at border.

text.p: Malaysia has tightened checks at its border with Thailand in a bid to stop thousands of Bangladeshis, stranded for weeks in Thai jungles, entering the country illegally, an official said on Wednesday.

"The government is aware and I don't think they can breach through now, because we have already stepped up our operations at the northern border," Tengku Zaman Tengku Hariff, a senior official of Malaysia's home ministry, told reporters.
There were "indications that the Thai government is also assisting" in the operations, he added.
Dhaka officials said on Tuesday the Bangladeshis were en route to Malaysia where they had hoped to find jobs.
About 300,000 Bangladeshis work in Malaysia, making them one of the largest expatriate communities, according to official statistics.
Many of the illegals were flown to Thailand by bogus employment agents who did not have work permits or necessary documents, they said.
Bangladesh's official BSS news agency put the number of stranded illegals at 50,000 and said they were "living a wretched and unbearable life in the jungles of Thailand".
Thailand's immigration chief in the southern province of Songhkla said he could not confirm the number.
"Figures are very difficult to verify," he said. "Some say 50,000, some 40,000, some 30,000. But I can say the number is substantial."

He said the Thai government had informed Malaysia it had issued 30,000 to 40,000 transit visas to Bangladeshi nationals since last year "but we don't know the exact number who actually left Thailand".
He said Thailand was the only known entry point into Malaysia for Bangladeshi illegals and the government had heard stories of Bangladeshis holed up in Thai jungles as early as last year.
He added that as long as the illegals did not cross the border "it's up to the Thai government to deal with them".

Bangladesh government officials said the country's High Commission in Kuala Lumpur had been told to make every effort to convince the Malaysian government to allow the immigrants to enter the country legally.
Last year, Malaysia built a three-metre (10-ft) high wall along parts of the border with Thailand to deter smugglers and stem the flow of illegal immigrants.
The Thai immigration chief in Songhkla said Thai authorities would arrest and deport any illegal immigrants as and when they were found.
More than 300 were already in police custody, he added.
